analytical_question: As of 2026-10-13, America/New_York, does this hypothetically authorized, isolated V2G configuration justify a bounded operational experiment while protecting delivery readiness?
general_et_finding: V2G requires bidirectional vehicle/equipment capability and utility-permitted grid export; V2B backup and ordinary managed charging are distinct uses. Technical capability does not establish broad commercial maturity: DOE describes vehicle grid-service incentive programs as not widely available.
application_finding: Grid-export learning requires an operational trial, not merely a non-export proof of concept. Managed charging is the strongest alternative for protecting route readiness without export; a V2G experiment is justified only if isolation and enforceable reserves contain delivery consequences.
organization_specific_finding: The stipulated permission, compatibility, warranty coverage, accepted terms, dedicated non-route vehicle, tested cutoff, and human stop control support bounded experimentation. The decisive reason is reversible learning without dependence on a delivery vehicle, not the organization's innovator posture.

evidence.claim: DOE distinguishes V2G grid export from V2B backup, identifies bidirectional capability and utility interconnection permission, and describes limited diffusion of vehicle grid-service incentives.
evidence.source_or_reference: DOE FEMP, Managed and Bidirectional Charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging — ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Supplied packet retrieved 2026-10-13; page publication date not stated.
evidence.notes: Live page corroborates the supplied packet; no historical snapshot was verified. It establishes neither this fleet's authorization nor profitability.

evidence.claim: DOE describes managed charging as considering vehicle energy needs and control objectives while supporting vehicle readiness.
evidence.source_or_reference: DOE FEMP, Managed and Bidirectional Charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging — ([energy.gov](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging))
evidence.date_or_recency: Supplied packet retrieved 2026-10-13; page publication date not stated.
evidence.notes: Selecting managed charging as the strongest alternative is an analytical inference, not evidence of this organization's savings.

evidence.claim: Trial-specific authorization, compatibility, warranty coverage, accepted payment/liability terms, vehicle isolation, reserve cutoff, and human stop control are stipulated.
evidence.notes: Not audited documents, observations of a real fleet, or field deployment evidence; profitability remains unproven.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Counter-case: if the objective is only reliable charging for deliveries, managed charging avoids export exposure and may make V2G experimentation unnecessary.
An isolated trial cannot establish fleet-wide economics, route reliability, or scalable implementation.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Confidence is high in the conditional teaching-case recommendation, not in real-world deployment readiness. Commercial value and transferability to delivery-assigned vehicles remain uncertain; no developments after the analysis cutoff are used.
value_opportunity_implication: The opportunity is operational learning about controllable export and actual pilot economics, not assumed savings. Compare incremental benefits and costs against managed charging before considering expansion.
risk_governance_implication: Maintaining authorization, covered duty cycles, vehicle isolation, and tested reserve/stop controls is a prerequisite to export. Stop export if reserve protection fails or the test vehicle becomes necessary for deliveries.
recommendation_management_implication: Bounded experiment: permit the stipulated isolated operational grid-export trial now, within its authorized scope and human stop authority; fleet-wide rollout remains blocked. Pass operating-capacity assessment and implementation ownership to the Organizational Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reverse to defer export if permission or warranty coverage lapses, reserve/stop control fails, or the test vehicle becomes delivery-critical.
Reassess expansion only after documented pilot economics and route-readiness evidence support a separately authorized larger scope.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: For a real deployment, obtain the actual trial-specific permission, compatibility evidence, warranty terms, and accepted liability agreement; teaching-case stipulations do not substitute for verification.
Abstain from fleet-wide adoption until economic results and readiness evidence from representative delivery operations are available.
